q1_issues.issue: The explicit adversative connective "but" is dropped: no surface-headed (But <clause1> <clause2>) atom is emitted, and neither clause's state is reified as a connective endpoint, so the stated relation between the two clauses is lost (no defeasible-exception construction consumes it here).

q2_gaps: free-choice "either one" as a standalone determiner-pronoun over an unmentioned pair — the disjunction section covers "either ... or", and the quantifier table has no entry for "either", so neither the both-conjuncts reading nor a QuantifierPhrase companion is specified
"the former" / "the latter" anaphora: nothing licenses recording which member of an introduced pair is first, so the ordering survives only as an untyped witness index
an elided comparative standard ("more concise" with the than-phrase omitted) — no rule says whether to supply the implicit standard or leave the second argument open
notes: Distributing "fine" to both witnesses is the free-choice reading and is defensible, and (More concise sk_thing_1 sk_thing_2) uses the surface adjective as the scale in surface argument order; the two antecedentless referents correctly fall back to the `thing` class.
